clue.text: Suggested unpretentiousness with no frills

indicators.note: frills are trimmings at the edges, so a word with no frills loses its outermost letters at each end

parts.note: lack of pretension is plainness

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a plain, frill-free style of living.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMPLICITY with its first and last letters stripped leaves IMPLICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied rather than stated outright, just as a hint is conveyed indirectly.

clue.text: Ignore dance number a company released

parts.note: a disco is a dance event

parts.note: a count is a total number
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm drops a dance track from its catalogue and people overlook it.
explanation.walkthrough: DISCO plus COUNT gives DISCOCOUNT; taking out one CO leaves DISCOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To discount a claim or possibility is to disregard it, treating it as unworthy of consideration.

clue.text: Officials sign name on books first

indicators.note: first puts the name abbreviation at the front, ahead of the other two pieces

the Old Testament, the usual crossword books
a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Office holders put their signatures in ledgers before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a verb about signing, but it is a star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are legal officers who certify documents and witness signatures.

clue.text: Plastic toy did something strange

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so these letters are remoulded into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A child's plastic toy behaved in an unexpected way.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is a peculiar or unusual thing, a curiosity that stands out as bizarre.

clue.text: Part of goal is to stop getting angry at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset places the word for being angry at the start, before the word for stopping

parts.note: cross means annoyed
to bar is to prevent or block

explanation.surface: Advice to a footballer: the trick to scoring is keeping your temper early on.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbar is the horizontal beam joining the top of the two goalposts in football.

clue.text: Regularly still dig clay to get mineral

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the phrase is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A digger keeps working the clay in search of a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Silica, silicon dioxide, is a hard mineral found as quartz and sand.

clue.text: Go to essentially imitate proteins found in regressive DNA

indicators.note: those centre letters are found inside the other piece
regressing means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: used as written, then turned around

parts.note: the middle letter of imitate is used
the two middle letters of proteins are used

explanation.surface: A scientist tries to mimic proteins encoded in DNA that runs backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: T (heart of imitate) and TE (heart of proteins) go into AND, which is DNA regressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it, so a synonym of go to.

clue.text: Volkswagen Polo discovered as girlfriend goes outside

indicators.note: goes outside says the girlfriend's abbreviation wraps around the uncovered letters

parts.note: GF is the common short form of girlfriend

parts.note: the two inner letters

explanation.surface: Someone's girlfriend found a Volkswagen Polo when she went outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volkswagen Polo' reads as one car, but Polo is wordplay and Volkswagen alone is the definition: the Golf is another VW model.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golf is a long-running hatchback model made by the German carmaker, so it is one example of that brand.

clue.text: Caught The Society Of Jesus for example, buying from a catalogue?

definitions.note: describes a method of buying rather than the act itself, hence the question mark

indicators.note: caught here means heard or picked up by ear, so the phrase is what is spoken rather than written

parts.words: The Society Of Jesus for example
parts.note: the Jesuits are a religious order of men only

explanation.surface: Someone spots Jesuits ordering goods from a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like an arrest or a cricket dismissal; it means heard. The Society of Jesus, the Jesuits, admits only men.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail order is the system of choosing goods from a printed catalogue and having them delivered by post.

clue.text: Keen on capturing rook as first piece

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so the outer word holds the chess piece abbreviation inside it

parts.note: being into something means being enthusiastic about it
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess player eager to take a rook as the first piece captured.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting makes 'piece' a chessman, but here it is a piece of music or writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a song or composition, the first part one hears.

clue.text: Some truly crazy material

indicators.note: some means a portion of what follows, so the letters are taken from inside the phrase

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict that a certain fabric is genuinely wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a trademarked stretchy synthetic fabric, the spandex used in sportswear.

clue.text: Not being affected by if it's open surprisingly

indicators.note: something that happens surprisingly comes out in an unexpected way, so these letters land in an unexpected order

parts.note: the fodder, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone unbothered whether a door is open or shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something regardless of an obstacle is doing it notwithstanding that obstacle, undeterred by it.

clue.text: Ridicule vineyard providing case of chardonnay bottles

parts.note: a cru is a French wine-growing estate

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the outer letters enclose the word for providing
the case of a word is its outer shell, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters
providing that means on condition, if

explanation.surface: A sneer at a vineyard selling cases of chardonnay in bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine words dress up abbreviations: CRU comes first, then C(IF)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To crucify someone in informal use is to criticise or mock them savagely.

clue.text: One who stays in bed by the sound of it?

parts.note: a border is a flower bed along the edge of a lawn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays in bed' suggests a lie-in; the bed is a garden border.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarder is a lodger or pupil who lives in someone's house or a school and is given meals.

clue.text: Looking up document containing one on the no-fly list?

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards
containing says the answer is held inside the next word's letters

parts.note: the fourth to sixth letters

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an airport security check, but the no-fly list is the flightless birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large Australian bird that cannot fly, so it belongs with the flightless species.

clue.text: Ultimately wanting 22 nudists at casting for play

indicators.note: casting is throwing or moulding afresh, so all these letters are thrown into a new order
ultimately wanting means lacking at the very end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the answer to 22 across
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: UNICORN loses its final N, then joins NUDISTS AT in the anagram; 'casting' reads as theatre auditions but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Andronicus is Shakespeare's early and bloodiest revenge tragedy.

clue.text: Trendy new hotel

parts.note: in means fashionable
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fashionable recently opened hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a small hotel or pub offering lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Just 17 incorrectly describing origami conclusively as martial art

indicators.note: letters set incorrectly are out of order
to describe a circle is to draw it round something, so the jumbled letters take in the final letter of origami

parts.note: used as written
the answer to clue 17 is INN

indicators.note: conclusively points to the final letter

parts.note: the last letter of origami is used

explanation.surface: A teen magazine wrongly describes paper folding as a fighting discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just 17' reads as the British teen magazine Just Seventeen, but 17 is the cross-reference to INN; 'describing' adds the end of origami to the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjitsu is the Japanese art of stealth and espionage practised by ninja, a form of martial art.

clue.text: Dietary option that's ordinary after cooking using swan finally for a King

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective; read it as describing such an option

for means in place of, so one letter swaps in where the royal letter was

parts.note: taken as written
R for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the bird is used

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A menu note on how a vegan dish is made from swan instead of a king's portion.
explanation.walkthrough: One R of ORDINARY is replaced by N, then the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-dairy food contains no milk products, a choice catering for vegans and the lactose intolerant.

clue.text: Cuts quickly!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: two strokes with an axe or knife
second meaning: a command to hurry up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an order to an editor or butcher to hurry; the repeated word is both literal chopping and pidgin for 'hurry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal exclamation urging someone to be fast, from pidgin English.

clue.text: Watch intervention that uses current to stop flood

parts.note: a spate is a sudden rush of water
electroconvulsive therapy, which passes an electric current through the brain

explanation.surface: Someone watches an electrical scheme intended to hold back floodwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' sounds like a river feature beside 'flood', but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to be an onlooker, observing an event such as a match.

clue.text: Military jacket ripped when leaders removed Scottish symbol

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters, and these are taken off

parts.note: a tunic is a close-fitting military jacket
torn means ripped

explanation.surface: A soldier's coat is torn once the officers have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: TUNIC and TORN each lose their first letter, giving UNIC and ORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is the national animal of Scotland and supports the Scottish royal arms.

clue.text: Sort of home and not home

parts.note: being in means being at home
away means absent from home

explanation.surface: A puzzling riddle about being both at home and out.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so to some extent, partly or somewhat, is to hedge with that phrase.

clue.text: Conclusion — having made good terms in our contract — promise not to talk

parts.note: omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it means the end or conclusion

parts.note: the last letters of our and contract

clue.text: Excuse starts in 5, 4, 3, 2, 1

indicators.note: starts means the first letter of each of the four answers named

parts.note: 5 refers to the answer of 5-down, CROSSBAR
the start of 4-down's answer, ODDITY
the start of 3-down's answer, NOTARIES
the start of 2-down's answer, DISCOUNT
here the number 1 is taken simply as the word one, not as a reference

explanation.definitionFit: To condone a fault is to excuse or overlook it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Ministers extremely cranky when taking on large amount of work

an erg is a unit of work or energy in physics

explanation.definitionFit: The clergy are the body of ordained ministers of a church, so the plural noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Period of calm to go over ideal serve by Henman

Tim Henman, the British tennis player

parts.note: PE is physical education, school games
or is gold in heraldry

C for clubs, the card suit

clue.text: Visiting Arsenal — City occasionally counter

clue.text: Sir Alan Parker on the radio, maybe to add positive spin?
